records.text:
1. Initial contrast-enhanced CT: Showed interruption of flow in right sigmoid and transverse sinuses
2. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT: Revealed tumor in jugular foramen extending into deep cervical region, medially displacing internal carotid artery
3. MRI findings:
      - Hypointensity on T1-weighted images
      - Iso-to hyperintensity on T2-weighted images
      - Smooth tumor rim enhancement on contrast-enhanced MRI
      Image Title: Tumor in jugular foramen
      Image Description: Tumor extending into deep cervical region without internal flow voids, surrounding internal carotid artery
- Pathological Findings:
      - Epithelioid cells with enlarged nuclei and eosinophilic/clear cytoplasm
      - Immunohistochemistry: Positive for HMB-45, Melan-A, α-SMA, TFE3; Negative for desmin, AE1/AE3, S-100 protein
      - Mitotic index: 2/10 HPF
      - MIB-1 labeling index: approximately 5%.

bindings.label: Hoarseness, dysphagia, vomiting, and headache, with hoarseness worsening at age 31
No personal or family history of tuberous sclerosis was reported
Initial symptoms improved with anticoagulant therapy but later worsened
Physical examination revealed paralysis of right cranial nerves IX to XII (Collet-Sicard syndrome)
MRI shows a jugular foramen tumor with smooth rim enhancement, deep cervical extension, surrounding the ICA, and no internal flow voids
Pathology shows epithelioid cells with HMB-45, Melan-A, TFE3 positive and S-100 negative, consistent with PEComa
Normal coagulation tests argue against hypercoagulability
CT sinus flow interruption is due to extrinsic compression rather than intrinsic thrombosis
Initial CT showed right sigmoid and transverse sinus flow interruption
Patient has PEComa (perivascular epithelioid cell tumor) of the jugular foramen/skull base
Immunofluorescence microscopy demonstrated linear IgA deposition along the basement membrane
